keyFindings.description: Fast-follow, not held. The nine agent-facing descriptions interpolate the constant, so each reads 'at most 32000 characters' where every other surface in this change writes '32,000' (packages/envoy/AGENTS.md:1828, packages/contracts/AGENTS.md:34, docs/site/.../dispatch/for-agents.md:101), and the same strings are baked into packages/claude-envoy/dist/{dispatch,envoy-channel,session-hook}.js. A formatted copy of the constant beside DISPATCH_BODY_MAX, then a bundle rebuild, fixes it. Wording class: no behaviour, no error hidden, no gate.

Fast-follow, not held. The write-time surfaces an agent reads - the dispatch comment and dispatch suggest descriptions, and skills/dispatch/, which does not mention the margin at all - raise the number without the anchored-comment margin clause this change added to docs/site/.../dispatch/for-agents.md:102-106 and packages/envoy/CHANGELOG.md:419-424, so an agent writing a cap-length anchored comment meets the byte bound as a 413 rather than as guidance. The architect's ruling named the docs site and the changelog and both carry it; extending it to the tool descriptions is beyond that ruling, and the docs site is the agents' guide, so the guidance exists. Offered as fast-follow and reported to the architect so it can override.

Fast-follow, not held. Both lines restate record.MessagePostLimit as the literal 31956, twice each (the bound and the message), where this change's own packages/daemon/internal/workflow/ready_test.go:269-278 took the opposite rule and derived it. The shape is pre-existing - the value was 1956 before and a shell proof cannot read a Go constant without new machinery - and both are soft, so drift warns rather than fails. One readonly near the top would halve the literals.
